en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape among all active volcanoes in the world.
The Cagayan River, located in northern Luzon, is the longest and largest river in the entire Philippine archipelago.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the smallest primates in the world and has enormous eyes.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller crater lake called Main Crater Lake.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Rafflesia, found in the rainforests of Luzon and Mindanao, produces the largest individual flower on Earth.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse marine life.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippines experiences two main monsoon winds called the cool northeast amihan and the rainy southwest habagat.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest reserves of nickel, a metal heavily mined in Palawan and Zambales.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
